input: Plain UTF-8 multi-game PGN exported from Chess.com, Lichess or another source. Mainline legal replay from the initial Standard position; variations/comments/NAGs do not contribute visits.
privacy: Files and normalized games remain in the browser worker for the session. No account connection, API downloads, model calls, server uploads or persistent storage. Clearing/reloading terminates the worker. Report download is explicit and contains summaries rather than raw PGNs.
eligibility: Completed known results and legal Standard mainlines with named players. Reject variants, setup/FEN games, unfinished or conflicting results, duplicate headers and illegal mainlines. Do not impose reference-corpus rating floors. Missing ratings and casual games are supported; unknown metadata stays unknown.
identity: Provider + native game ID from recognized Site/Link URLs. Chess.com live/daily namespaces stay separate; Lichess uses the first eight game-ID characters. Conflicting provider/native-ID headers are rejected. Generic fallback is SHA256 of normalized player names, date and UCI mainline; source-file SHA256 is separate.
deduplication: Semantic fingerprint of normalized players, UCI moves and completed result excludes comments, variations, NAGs and other optional metadata. Same identity with equal fingerprint counts once; any differing fingerprint withholds all copies of that identity as conflicts. Provider identities never collapse across platforms. First copy supplies optional metadata.
reconciliation: Framed records = accepted unique games + duplicate copies + conflicting copies + rejected records. Failed framing imports no partial file and its unframed records are outside that count. Invalid UTF-8, byte/file/game/ply/variation-depth caps, cancellation or timeout retain no partial session.
player_selection: Explicit selected player per provider; NFC lowercase matching within that provider. A matching name on another provider is not automatically the same person. White first; matched Black games and unmatched-player records are reported separately.
personal_denominator: All selected valid completed Standard White games after explicit date/time-control/rated filters, including short games. Date-filtered undated games are excluded visibly. An optional minimum-20-ply comparison filter has its own exclusion count.
position_identity: First four canonical FEN fields with legal en passant; SHA256 truncated to 24 hex characters, matching the checked public reference. Preserve full FEN separately. Draw counters/history are not part of the recognition key.
position_metrics: One earliest eligible visit per game/position. Frequency = position games / selected White games. Acyclic route count excludes any repeated-position prefix. Alternative-route share = 1 - largest acyclic route game count / (position games - repetition-prefix games), null for zero acyclic games.
reference_scope: Selected first-N published study positions, N=1..20, for one cohort/view/ranking. Coverage is the union of selected White games reaching those boards. No match means not in this selected set, not unknown in the full corpus or out of theory.
route_comparison: First differing move while the selected published route examples still define a next move, within the first 20 plies. An example ending stops comparison; it is not a departure. A later canonical White decision matching a selected board counts as re-entry. This is not a move-quality or mistake metric.
metadata: Date is a valid UTCDate or Date header, otherwise null; do not infer UTC time. Rated status uses explicit Rated true/false or Rated/Casual/Unrated Event prefixes; Chess.com branding alone does not establish rated status. TimeControl is retained without guessed speed/rating comparability.
limits_of_inference: Personal samples and public reference cohorts differ. Coverage is a descriptive count of the selected reference set. No engine evaluation, learning-gain claim, causal result comparison, username downloads or private-game authentication. Generic fingerprints cannot resolve every missing-ID ambiguity.
